summary: One system for booking, check-in, charts and payments, with a phone assistant that books appointments on its own.
challenge: Booking, front-desk check-in, doctor charts and billing lived in separate places: a website, paper forms, a card reader and a billing tool. Every appointment meant re-entering the same patient several times, and every reminder was a phone call someone had to make.
approach: We mapped the clinic's day from the first booking to the paid invoice and built one system around it. Patients use their phones. Doctors see their day on one screen. Reminders and phone bookings run without the front desk.
built: Patients book, reschedule and cancel online, and complete intake forms before the visit. A lobby screen tells the front desk when someone has arrived. Doctors see their day, the chart, the visit history and the bill in one place. Admins run the schedule, services, providers, invoices, patient credit and US insurance claims (CMS-1500). Cards can be taken online, by link, on a reader or from a saved card. Confirmations and reminders go out by text and email on their own. An AI phone assistant books callers into real open slots, and each doctor's Google Calendar stays in sync both ways.

results.label: Booking, check-in, charts and payments sit in the same place.
A patient is entered once. Reminders and phone bookings run without the front desk.

summary: A marketplace where brands pay for promotional videos and verified creators get paid in their own currency, including mobile money.
challenge: Brands across African markets wanted many creators to promote a product at once, but had no reliable way to pay dozens of people across countries, or to be sure each video was actually posted. Creators needed to know they would be paid.
approach: Brand funds go into a wallet. Each video is checked before the creator is paid, and creators withdraw to a bank account or mobile money. Every movement of money is recorded, so balances can always be checked.
built: A brand signs up, verifies the business, and tops up a wallet by card or bank. They build a campaign and see the price before it launches, then follow every creator's submission and status. Creators join with verified TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and Facebook accounts, take work from a job feed, submit the video and see their earnings in the app. Payouts go to a bank account or to MTN, Vodafone and AirtelTigo mobile money. The platform handles NGN, GHS, KES, ZAR and USD with live exchange rates. An operations dashboard covers verifications, video approval, payouts and reports, and brands can give team roles, with two-factor login for everyone.

results.label: Each video is reviewed before the creator is paid.
Creators withdraw to a bank or to mobile money, in NGN, GHS, KES, ZAR and USD.

anonymousName: A leadership learning platform in Ghana
summary: An executive learning platform: apply, pay, join a live cohort and finish with a certificate, all in one place.
challenge: Leaders had conviction but no structured place to practise it. Applications, payments, class schedules and materials were spread across forms, chats and documents, which made cohorts hard to run and harder to finish.
approach: We built the whole path in one product: programme page, application, payment, cohort and certificate. Facilitators run their classes from the same system.
built: The public site has programme pages and an online application. Checkout runs through Paystack, priced in cedis for Ghana and US dollars elsewhere, with payment plans that staff review. Learners move week by week through live classes, recordings, assignments, quizzes and reading, and a leadership self-assessment builds a personal profile. Facilitators take attendance, grade work, post announcements and open each week of the course. Admins handle applications, cohorts, programmes and offline payments. Certificates are PDFs, and there is an alumni area.

results.label: Apply, pay, join the cohort and finish with a certificate in the same product.
A learner sees the class, the assignment and what is due, without chasing files.

anonymousName: A counseling platform in the United States
summary: A software platform that lets any counseling organisation run its programmes, clients, referral partners and payments under its own brand.
challenge: Counseling teams, the people in their programmes and the agencies that refer them were each keeping their own record, in spreadsheets, on paper and over the phone. Nobody shared one current picture of a case, and every status update meant another call.
approach: It began as the system we built for a single counseling clinic. We turned it into a platform any counseling organisation can sign up for, each with its own branded portal and web address.
built: A counseling organisation signs up on its own, with its branding, letterhead and web address. Staff get a Today dashboard, a client directory, sessions, groups, attendance and a calendar. Clients use a portal for intake, sessions, documents and payments, and referral partners submit referrals and receive progress updates. Payments can be taken by card through Square, with optional Cash App and Venmo, plus reminders. Monthly progress reports and completion certificates are PDFs. Email and text reminders, Zoom sessions and Google Calendar sync sit in the same system. Operators manage organisations, plans and billing, and edit the public site. The interface is in English, Spanish and French, with authenticator-app sign-in, encrypted secrets and nightly encrypted backups.

results.label: Staff, clients and referral partners share the current picture of a case.
Each organisation signs up with its own name, letterhead and web address.

anonymousName: A multilingual ministry in the United States
summary: A ministry website in four languages, with online giving and a staff desk that lets the team run the site without a developer.
challenge: Teaching, help requests, trainings and giving were spread across channels, and every content change needed technical help. The ministry also serves readers who don't read English first.
approach: We gave the staff a private desk where they can change every page, notice and story themselves. Help requests and gifts arrive there too, away from the public site.
built: The public site is in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. People can request prayer and pastoral support, browse a teaching library with videos and trainings, and sign up for trips. Giving is one-time or monthly by card, and an incomplete gift can be finished later. There is a newsletter people can join, and the team can send it. Mission Desk is the staff workspace for content, messages, help requests, gifts and the newsletter. Search, share previews and a sitemap help the site get found.

results.label: The public site reads in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese.
The team changes pages, notices and stories without calling a developer.

summary: A leadership website for programmes, projects and stories, with a way to take part and a way to give.
challenge: Programmes, stories and invitations to take part sat in documents and social posts. A visitor opening the old site had to piece together what COME does, and what to do next.
approach: We built pages the team can update as cohorts, events and teaching change. Programmes, projects, stories and giving sit on one site, in the organisation's own voice.
built: The home page introduces COME. Programme pages explain the pathways. Projects and insights hold the work and the stories, and Our story has its own page. A visitor can give from the menu on any page. The Academy work we still hold with COME sits alongside this site.

results.label: Programmes, projects, stories and giving sit together.
A visitor can see what COME does, take part, or give from the menu.

anonymousName: A counseling clinic in the United States
summary: A private platform where a counseling clinic, its clients and referral partners manage programmes, sessions, payments and progress reports.
challenge: The clinic runs court-referred and voluntary programmes. Each case needs enrollment, attendance, payments and written progress, and referral partners such as probation officers and attorneys need accurate updates. That work was being assembled by hand from a calendar, a payment tool, paper intake and report documents.
approach: We designed for privacy and calm. Three separate signed-in areas (staff, clients, partners) each see only what they should. The interface stays quiet enough for a clinician between sessions.
built: Staff see clients, referrals, groups, programmes, assessments and the calendar on one dashboard, and attendance tracking follows up with people who stop coming. Clients complete intake paperwork with a signature, see sessions, book assessments and pay online. Referral partners refer clients, follow cases and download reports. Progress reports and programme completion certificates are PDFs. Reminders for sessions, payments and case updates go by email and text. Sessions can be in person, by phone or by video. The interface is in English, Spanish and French. Access is by role, with an audit log, and texting stays off until a privacy agreement is in place.

results.label: Staff, clients and partners each see only what they should.
Attendance, payments and progress reports come from the same record.

summary: The learning space for the Elevate Tribe Mentorship Program. A learner signs in, opens their courses and sees what is due.
challenge: The programme had courses to teach and work for learners to hand in. That needed one signed-in place, so a learner could see their classes, the next assignment and the calendar without asking someone to send a link.
approach: We set the programme up in Moodle, under the Elevate Tribe name. A learner signs in with their ID and lands on a dashboard. The courses open from there.
built: The sign-in asks for the learner's ID. The dashboard shows the coming week, including assignments for Academic Excellence and Spiritual Excellence, and a calendar for new events. My courses lists the two tracks in the Elevate Tribe Mentorship Program: Academic Excellence, on mastery, discipline and learning, and Spiritual Excellence, on character and faith. The same sign-in is where the programme is taught.

results.label: A learner opens their courses, the next assignment and the calendar from the dashboard.
Academic Excellence and Spiritual Excellence are listed in My courses.

summary: A services site for data and training work with businesses, nonprofits and faith organisations.
challenge: The team could do the work. The site did not say what that work was. A visitor had to guess whether they needed training, data analysis, or both, and how to ask.
approach: We split that into pages a visitor can read in order: who the team is, what they do, and how to start. Each service is written out on its own.
built: The home page states the work. About introduces the team. Services is written for businesses, nonprofits and faith organisations, and includes faith-based data analysis, using records a ministry already keeps, such as attendance and giving. FAQs and a contact page cover the usual questions. Get started is the way to ask for a conversation.

results.label: A visitor can read the services for businesses, nonprofits and faith organisations.
Get started is the page where someone asks for a conversation.

summary: A course site for Twi and Fante, in person and online, with a straight way to register.
challenge: People in Ghana and in the diaspora wanted structured Twi and Fante. The courses existed. Packages, age groups, and the choice between in person and online were explained in too many places, so signing up took longer than it should.
approach: We organised the site the way a new student thinks: language, level, format, then register. The same pages work for a traveller on a phone and a parent booking a child.
built: The home page announces the next group start and a way to register. Courses cover Twi and Fante, from beginner to advanced, in a group or one to one, in person or online. About TLC, cultural immersion and the TLC Foundation each have their own page. Sign up sits in the menu on every page.

results.label: Language, level and format lead to sign up, in person or online.
Beginner to advanced, in a group or one to one.

summary: The portal where a client sees each piece of work, the hours it took, and the amount, before they approve it.
challenge: Updates and bills were easy to lose across messages. A client had no single place to see what had shipped and what it cost.
approach: Scopewise is the portal we use with our own clients. We log the work as it happens. The client opens the same record, sees the hours and the amount, and approves from there.
built: A client signs in to see the work before they approve it. The work log shows the date, the work, the kind of change, the hours and the amount. The same portal holds the review queue, requests, clients and systems, billing, an activity log, AI spending and settings. A public link opens the record a client is reviewing.

results.label: The client sees the work, the hours and the amount before they approve it.
Updates and amounts stay in the portal, instead of across messages.

summary: A company site for HVAC, industrial refrigeration, ventilation and MEP work in Ghana, with a clear way to ask for a quote.
challenge: Ikedoo works across several trades, from refrigeration to full building services. A visitor needed one place to see which trade they needed, and a direct way to ask for a quote.
approach: The home page leads with the company name and the trades. Services, the company story and the quote request each have their own page, so a visitor can read first and write in when they are ready.
built: The home page names HVAC, industrial refrigeration, ventilation and MEP, and offers a quote. Services describes the work for commercial, industrial and institutional buildings, from assessment and design through installation, commissioning and maintenance. About introduces the company. Contact is where a visitor writes in.

results.label: HVAC, refrigeration, ventilation and MEP are named on the home page.
A visitor can read the work, then ask for a quote.

anonymousName: A French podcast and resource site
summary: A French site for a podcast, free resources and training on autism, written for families, professionals and institutions.
challenge: Families and professionals needed one place, in French, to listen, read and find support. The podcast, the guides and the training were easy to miss when they lived in separate posts.
approach: We gave the podcast, the resources and the services each their own page. A visitor can listen, download a guide, or write in from the same site.
built: The site is in French. The home page introduces the podcast and a way to write in. The podcast page explains the show, on autism through science, lived experience and culture, and links out to where the episodes play. Resources holds free guides, videos and tools for families and professionals. Services covers support, training and awareness for parents, professionals and institutions, including applied behaviour analysis, with African and diasporic life kept in view.

results.label: The podcast, the free guides and the training sit together.
A visitor can play an episode, open a guide, or ask for support from the same site.

anonymousName: A parts and motorcycle company in Togo
summary: A point of sale for a parts and motorcycle company in Togo. The counter, the warehouse and the stock reports all use the same system.
challenge: Selling a part, sending stock to an agency and knowing what the warehouse holds were all part of one working day. The people at the counter and the people in the office needed the same products and the same prices.
approach: ECADIF is that system, in French. A person signs in with their role. From there they can sell parts or motos, follow stock as it moves, and open a report for the period they choose.
built: A person signs in with their role: sales, cashier, warehouse, director, accountant or stock manager. There is a sales screen for parts and one for motos. The product list shows the buy price, the wholesale price and the retail price in CFA francs. Stock by agency, replenishment history, transfers and orders sit with a client list. The stock control screen shows the value of the stock, the units, and what came in and went out.

results.label: The counter, the warehouse and the office use the same products and prices.
Stock value, units, and what came in and went out are on one screen.
